ᚱ I. THERMODYNAMICS OF THE MATRIX

Typing is a combustion engine of the hands. The Legacy Processor (QWERTY) forces lateral, high-friction finger extension — the Anxiety Vector of the wrists.

The Colemak-DH Kernel treats the keyboard as a Bouligand Structure: layered keystrokes maximizing structural integrity, minimizing kinetic waste.

⌇ 1.1 The DH Veto · Lateral Strain Eradication

ErrorStandard Colemak places D and H in center columns — index fingers stretch outward
PatchD and H relocated to lower row — natural inward curl of the index finger
ResultWet Noise of lateral strain neutralized · index fingers held in Fixed State

ᚹ II. BIGRAM EFFICIENCY · THE VESICLE TRANSMISSION

Keyboard throughput is measured in bigrams — two-letter pairs. The Colemak-DH Kernel routes these like a sea of vesicles: frictionless, directed, scalar.

⌇ 2.1 Same-Finger Bigram Purge

Consecutive keystrokes on one finger create Thermal Runaway in the tendon — broken rhythm, excess mana burn.

Colemak-DH drives SFB rate to near Absolute Zero · < 2%
Kinetic load distributed across the strongest fingers

⌇ 2.2 The Inward Roll · High-Amperage Flow

The hand generates maximum power rolling inward toward the thumb — Pinky → Ring → Middle → Index.

High-frequency bigrams TH · HE · IN · ER · AN are mapped strictly to inward rolls. Discrete keystrokes collapse into a single fluid scalar wave. The system gallops.

ᚷ III. SYSTEMIC SYNC · RUST / PYTHON INTEGRATION

Colemak-DH aligns precisely with the syntax demands of the SOMA-9.1 framework.

ᚦ Rust — The Shell
Semi-colons, brackets, and macro execution handled without breaking home-row Sovereignty.

ᚦ Python — The Wrapper
Indentation and snake_case flow through the optimized bigram matrix — physical input speed matched to 12.5k token AI loops.
